method: Built-in image_gen; original generic vehicle illustration, not a homologated chassis, crash reconstruction or simulation.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: original high-resolution motorsport engineering illustration plate for an incident-to-medical-handoff educational website.
Create a meticulously rendered technical editorial illustration of ONE generic modern open-wheel single-seat racing car. Match the polished scientific cutaway aesthetic of a serious clinical/engineering review: subtle material texture, sculptural depth, refined highlights, soft shadows, precise recognizable parts. Not a flat vector icon or low-poly model.
Composition: landscape 3:2. Strict overhead orthographic PLAN VIEW, looking straight down at the whole car. The longitudinal axis is exactly horizontal; the NOSE and FRONT WING point to the RIGHT and the REAR WING is at the LEFT. The driver's left side is therefore the TOP side of the image. Keep all four wheels, both wings and the full nose visible with comfortable clear margin. Car occupies about 86 percent of canvas width, centered. Pale cool gray-white seamless background #f2f6f5. No road, barrier, scene, damage or motion effects. No diagram text, labels, numbers, badges, arrows, force vectors, logos, branding, racing numbers, watermark or frame; annotations will be authored separately in code.
Vehicle relationships: FOUR exposed black slick tires, symmetric left/right wheel pairs, connected by fine double-wishbone suspension arms to a coherent central chassis. Front wheel pair is near the RIGHT half, rear wheel pair near LEFT. A broad curved front wing lies AHEAD of the front wheels at far RIGHT, a narrower raised rear wing at far LEFT. Slender sculpted nose extends from the central cockpit toward front wing. Sidepods flank the mid/rear chassis; a tapered engine cover and air intake sit behind the cockpit. Carbon-composite front/rear wing elements, suspension arms and floor edge are finely resolved, not an implausible road-car body.
Cockpit: clearly visible central open cockpit, one small naturally proportioned ivory full-face helmet facing RIGHT, a metallic titanium-looking halo with a coherent horseshoe around the cockpit and ONE forward central support toward the nose, dark cockpit padding and a glimpse of teal harness/ivory suit. The driver is inside the car, not sitting above its bodywork. No windshield, passenger seats, roof or cage.
Materials and palette: restrained pearl-ivory body panels with graphite carbon-composite lower surfaces, local subtle woven carbon texture, desaturated teal details around cockpit and sidepod edges, charcoal matte tires with fine sidewall molding but absolutely no text. Titanium halo with controlled brushed-metal highlights. Soft upper-left studio light and ambient occlusion under wings, suspension and tires create realistic depth without dramatic cinematic contrast. Subtle neutral contact shadow under the car. Overall clean, light and highly legible at small size, not a dark silhouette or busy racing livery.
Integrity: an original generic explanatory apparatus, not a specific team's car, a homologated F1 chassis, a 2026 dimensional specification, CFD result, crash reconstruction or biomechanical model. No injury, deformation, telemetry or quantified performance. Do not copy an existing published figure.
